questions.text: Suppose that [latex]f: \mathbb{R} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}[/latex] is a continuous function on the interval [-3,3] and a differentiable function in the interval (-3,3) such that for every [latex]x[/latex] in the interval, [latex]f'(x) \leq 2[/latex]. If [latex]f(-3) =7[/latex], then [latex]f(3) [/latex] is at most __________
questions.solution:
By the mean value theorem, [latex]f(3)-f(-3)=f'(c)\cdot6\le2\times6=12[/latex].

[latex]f(3)\le7+12=19[/latex]

Answer: 19

questions.text: Suppose that P is a 4x5 matrix such that every solution of the equation Px=0 is a scalar multiple of [latex]\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 5 & 4 &3 & 1 \end{bmatrix}^T[/latex]. The rank of P is _______
questions.solution:
All solutions of Px = 0 are multiples of one vector [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] nullity = 1.
P has 5 columns, so by rank-nullity: rank = 5 [latex]-[/latex] 1 = 4.

Answer: 4

questions.text:
Consider the following matrix.
[latex]\begin{pmatrix} 0 & 1 & 1 & 1\\ 1& 0& 1 & 1\\ 1& 1 & 0 & 1 \\1 & 1 & 1 & 0 \end{pmatrix}[/latex]
The largest eigenvalue of the above matrix is __________.
questions.solution:
The matrix is [latex]J-I[/latex], where J is the 4 [latex]\times[/latex] 4 all-ones matrix.
Eigenvalues of J: 4, 0, 0, 0. Subtracting 1: 3, [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]1, [latex]-[/latex]1.

Largest = 3

Answer: 3

questions.text:
Consider the following expression.
[latex]\lim_{x\rightarrow-3}\frac{\sqrt{2x+22}-4}{x+3}[/latex]
The value of the above expression (rounded to 2 decimal places) is ___________.
questions.solution:
At x = [latex]-[/latex]3 the numerator is [latex]\sqrt{16}-4=0[/latex] (form 0/0). Use L'Hospital:
[latex]\frac{d}{dx}\sqrt{2x+22}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2x+22}}[/latex] [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] at x = [latex]-[/latex]3: [latex]\frac14=0.25[/latex]

Answer: 0.25

questions.text: If [latex]x+2 y=30[/latex],then [latex]\left(\frac{2 y}{5}+\frac{x}{3}\right)+\left(\frac{x}{5}+\frac{2 y}{3}\right)[/latex] will be equal to
questions.solution:
Group the terms: [latex]\frac{x+2y}{5}+\frac{x+2y}{3}=\frac{30}{5}+\frac{30}{3}=6+10=16[/latex]

Answer: 16
